identity.package: module (shield PCB that stacks on the Uno via pin headers, with a mini breadboard stuck to the top)

function.one_sentence_plain_english: A blank circuit board that plugs on top of the UNO and gives you a small breadboard and solder pads, so you can build a circuit without a tangle of loose wires.
function.what_it_is_used_for: Building semi-permanent or compact circuits: stick components onto the small breadboard on top for a solderless build, or solder parts directly onto the prototyping grid underneath for something sturdier.
function.how_it_works_briefly: The shield's header pins on the underside plug straight into the Uno's own headers, extending every Uno pin up to a matching row of holes on top of the shield right next to the mini breadboard, so wiring a part is a short hop instead of a long wire run. The shield has no chip of its own, so its 32 header pins are a straight mechanical pass-through of the Uno's own power, analog, and digital headers.

pins.pin_1_identification: There is no dedicated pin 1. Orientation is fixed because the header spacing only stacks onto an Uno one way, keyed against the USB/power-jack end of the Uno like any other shield. Pin 1 of the power header (NC) sits nearest the USB connector end of the board.

electrical.operating_voltage: same as whatever the Uno underneath supplies (5V logic at the shield's header)
electrical.typical_current: negligible; the shield's own onboard LED circuit draws a few mA when used
electrical.interface: none (passive pass-through board, no chip of its own)

key_specs.onboard_extras: 2 LEDs (red, green) each with a matching resistor, 1 reset button, 1 general-purpose push button, two 0.1uF capacitors, a surface-mount pad area for chips up to 14-pin SOIC, gold-plated header pads, 0.1in x 0.1in prototyping grid, and a pass-through ICSP header (2x3, 6 pins: CIPO, +5V, SCK, COPI, RESET, GND) so another shield or an AVR programmer can stack on top; the ICSP header is separate from, and not counted in, the 32-pin power/analog/digital header

visual_identification.shape_and_size: A rectangular PCB the same footprint as the Uno (about 7cm x 5.5cm) with two rows of female header sockets on the underside that plug straight down onto the Uno's pins, and a small breadboard (about 4.8cm x 3.4cm) stuck on top with its own grid of tiny insertion holes.
visual_identification.color_and_markings: PCB color usually matches other boards in the kit (commonly blue or red); the mini breadboard on top is white plastic with a printed red stripe (positive rail) and blue stripe (negative rail) along its edges. The header sockets are silkscreened with the mirrored Uno pin names: SCL, SDA, AREF, GND, 13 down to 8 on one row, 7 down to 0 continuing it, and IOREF, RESET, 3V3, 5V, GND, GND, VIN plus 0 through 5 (analog) along the opposite edge.
visual_identification.printed_text_to_look_for: A grid of prototyping pads near the header edges, plus a small reset button and an unlabeled general-purpose push button near one corner, and the pin names above each header row (SCL/SDA/AREF/GND/13-8/7-0 on the digital side, IOREF/RESET/3V3/5V/GND/GND/VIN/A0-A5 on the power/analog side).
easily_confused_with: A full-size solderless breadboard (much bigger, no header pins to plug into a board)
A bare Uno shield with no breadboard on top
A perfboard/stripboard (bare copper pads, no adhesive breadboard on top)

example_connections.uno_pin: GND (shield header pin 6 or 7, mirrors Uno GND)

required_extra_parts: jumper wires or direct component leads to use the mini breadboard or solder pads
wiring_to_uno.arduino_library: none; it is a passive board

hazards: Misaligning the header pins when pressing the shield onto the Uno can bend a pin
Careless soldering on the prototyping grid can bridge adjacent pads and short a signal to power or ground
handling_notes: Line up the header sockets carefully before pressing down; press evenly, not on one corner
Unplug USB power before attaching or removing the shield
common_mistakes: Assuming the mini breadboard's power rails are automatically connected to the Uno's 5V/GND (they are not, until you jumper them yourself)
Forgetting the shield adds height, which can make some enclosures not fit

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: Nothing on the shield's breadboard works
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: The breadboard's power rails were never jumpered to the Uno's 5V/GND pins
symptoms_and_causes.check: Run a jumper wire from a 5V pin on the shield header to the breadboard's + rail, and GND to the - rail, then re-check

symptoms_and_causes.symptom: Uno stops responding after attaching the shield
symptoms_and_causes.likely_cause: A bent or misaligned header pin is shorting two signals together
symptoms_and_causes.check: Remove the shield and inspect the header pins for bending before reseating

troubleshooting.how_to_test_with_a_multimeter: With the shield seated and the Uno powered, measure continuity between any GND point on the shield's header and the Uno's own GND pin; you should read near 0 ohm, confirming a solid connection.

confidence.notes: Second research pass. The shield has no chip of its own, so its 32 header pins (8 power, 6 analog, 18 digital including GND, AREF, SDA, SCL) are a direct mechanical mirror of the Uno's own headers. This pass confirmed that layout position-by-position against Arduino's own official UNO Rev3 pinout PDF (content.arduino.cc/assets/Pinout-UNOrev3_latest.pdf) and cross-checked it against Adafruit's official Proto Shield for Arduino product guide, whose fabrication print and photos show a UNO proto shield's silkscreen carrying the identical SCL/SDA/AREF/GND/digital/power/analog pin names in the same order, plus a separate pass-through ICSP header not counted in the 32-pin total. Price and product page were re-verified today against a live US retailer (ProtoSupplies, protosupplies.com) selling the same style of shield for $2.95; the previously-cited Robot Pi Shop price ($3.99) was not re-fetched this pass and is kept only as supplier context. ELEGOO still does not appear to sell this exact prototype shield as a separate product outside the kit, so manufacturer and MPN remain generic/unconfirmed, which is why overall confidence is medium rather than high despite the pinout now being fully confirmed.
